Spec 05

The document

The UI DNA document

An interface described the way an engineer needs it to rebuild it: what is on the page, how it is laid out, which values repeat, how it reacts, and what could not be observed.

Schema 0.3.0uidna-schemaZod · JSON Schema · TypeScript

The schema is published as uidna-schema (Zod, JSON Schema and TypeScript types) and versioned with dnaVersion. It is framework neutral: nothing in it mentions React, Tailwind or any other output framework.

A complete, validated example produced from Fixture A lives in docs/examples/fixture-a.dna.json: one viewport (390 px) and four safe clicks (the hamburger and the three accordion items), five states and five transitions. The snippets below are abbreviated illustrations of the same shapes, not verbatim copies.

05.1Provenance

Every measured or inferred value is wrapped:

json

{
  "value": "248px",
  "provenance": {
    "kind": "measured",
    "source": "computed-style",
    "stateId": "st_01",
    "viewport": { "width": 1280, "height": 800 },
    "evidenceId": "ev_3f9a1c7b2d4e",
    "capturedAt": "2026-10-13T17:29:00.000Z",
    "confidence": 0.98
  }
}
kindmeaningallowed sources
measuredread directly from the browser (a computed style, a box, an AX node)computed-style, bounding-box, a11y-tree, screenshot, network
observedseen to happen (a transition after a click, a layout change at a width)same as measured, mostly interaction
inferredwritten by the host agent through annotate_dnaagent only, and agent is only ever inferred
unknownnot obtained; carries a reason and value is nulloptional source hint

Measured wins over observed, observed over inferred. The instrument never writes inferred. An agent annotation never replaces a measured value: it is stored next to it under annotation, so both readings survive.

json

{
  "value": "#2f5bea",
  "provenance": { "kind": "measured", "source": "computed-style", "capturedAt": "…", "confidence": 1 },
  "annotation": {
    "value": "brand-primary",
    "provenance": { "kind": "inferred", "source": "agent", "capturedAt": "…", "confidence": 0.8, "rationale": "matches the logo" }
  }
}

05.2Top-level shape

sectionwhat it holds
dnaVersionsemver of the schema the document follows
targetURL or CDP target, scan id, time, viewports, budget limits and usage, tool version
apppages, routes, shared layouts (landmark regions), navigation edges discovered from links (recorded, not followed)
statescaptured states (one per page × viewport × moment) and the transitions between them
componentsfingerprinted component candidates and their instances
visualtoken clusters with evidence, and layout constraints per container node
behaviorevent → transition rules, observed by the explorer or inferred by the agent
assetsfonts, images, SVGs with origin and authorization status
limitationswhat was not observed, not accessible or not reconstructable, each with a reason
evidenceindex of evidence ids to artifact paths
annotationslog of agent patches applied through annotate_dna

Documents are validated on every read and write. Cross-references (state ids in transitions, definition ids in instances, style ids in nodes) must resolve; an invalid document is never stored.

05.3States and nodes

A state is one page at one viewport at one moment. Base states are the page as loaded; derived states follow a transition and point at their parent.

Each state carries its normalized node tree. Nodes are elements only, in document order, with a structural path (element-child indices from <body>, e.g. 1/2/0), the tag, allowlisted attributes, own text, the bounding box in page coordinates (or null when not rendered), a styleId into the state's deduplicated style table, the computed accessibility role and name, and accessibility properties. Styles are filtered to the rendering properties listed in src/browser/style-properties.ts, with user-agent defaults dropped.

Because every node of a state was captured together, nodes share the state's single provenance instead of carrying one each. Values derived from nodes (tokens, layout constraints, component boxes) are wrapped individually.

Content of a closed <details> element (everything but its summary) is recorded with box: null and visible: false even when Chromium keeps a retained layout box for it, so a derived state that opens the panel shows the panel's nodes becoming visible.

Tokens are measured over every state, including hover and focus states. Layout constraints and component instances are measured over base states only; derived states repeat the same structure and would multiply the document by the number of recorded interactions.

json

{
  "id": "n7",
  "parentId": "n3",
  "path": "0/0/1",
  "depth": 3,
  "tag": "button",
  "role": "button",
  "name": "Open menu",
  "attrs": { "class": "nav-toggle", "type": "button", "aria-expanded": "false", "aria-controls": "primary-menu", "aria-label": "Open menu" },
  "text": null,
  "box": { "x": 326, "y": 16, "width": 40, "height": 40 },
  "styleId": "a1b2c3d4e5f6",
  "a11y": { "expanded": false, "focusable": true, "nth": 0 },
  "visible": true,
  "interactive": true,
  "inForm": false,
  "childIds": ["n8", "n9", "n10"]
}

The role tree is the flattened list of nodes with a role; its digest identifies a state's accessible structure, and the DOM digest identifies its markup. Two captures with equal digests are the same state.

05.4Transitions

A transition records an action on a node of one state and the state it led to:

json

{
  "id": "tr_01",
  "from": "st_03",
  "action": { "type": "click", "target": { "nodeId": "n7", "nodePath": "0/0/1", "role": "button", "name": "Open menu", "tag": "button", "nth": 0 } },
  "to": "st_04",
  "sideEffects": false,
  "network": { "requests": 0, "nonGet": 0 },
  "revert": { "method": "toggle", "succeeded": true },
  "change": { "domChanged": true, "roleTreeChanged": true, "screenshotChanged": true, "changedNodeIds": ["n7", "n11"] },
  "provenance": { "kind": "observed", "source": "interaction", "stateId": "st_03", "capturedAt": "…", "confidence": 1 }
}

sideEffects is true when the action caused a non-GET request or a navigation; such actions are never repeated. Skipped interactions are not transitions: they are reported as unknowns with their reason by explore_interactions.

05.5Components

Component candidates come from fingerprints: the normalized structure (tags and roles to a limited depth, text and images abstracted), a coarse style class and the root role. Class names and text are not part of the fingerprint, so three cards with different copy match. A definition lists its instances per state, the props that vary between instances (text, image, link), style variants and a confidence derived from structural and style agreement. Naming is left to the agent; generatedName is a placeholder.

05.6Tokens

Tokens are clusters of measured values. A cluster lists every member value with its sample count, the properties it came from and the spread of the cluster. Values are only merged when the clustering evidence supports it; the token's confidence is the share of the representative member. Breakpoints are observed, not measured: a viewport width is a breakpoint token when the layout at that width differs from the next wider one.

json

{
  "id": "tok_color_01",
  "kind": "color",
  "generatedName": "color-01",
  "value": { "value": "#1b1f2a", "provenance": { "kind": "measured", "source": "computed-style", "capturedAt": "…", "confidence": 1 } },
  "cluster": { "sampleCount": 23, "members": [{ "value": "rgb(27, 31, 42)", "count": 23 }], "properties": ["color"] },
  "usage": { "count": 23, "stateIds": ["st_01", "st_02", "st_03"] }
}

05.7Behavior, assets, limitations

A behavior rule pairs an event on a target with the transition it produced and the effects seen in the DOM (an attribute toggled, a node shown or hidden, a class toggled, a style change). Rules derived from recorded transitions are observed; rules written by the agent are inferred.

Assets carry their origin (same-origin, cross-origin, inline, data) and an authorization that starts as unknown. Only the user or the agent can set authorized; unauthorized assets become labeled placeholders in generated projects.

Limitations are first-class: not-observed (a lazy-loaded region below the capture height, an interaction skipped by policy), not-accessible (an iframe that was not entered), not-reconstructable (inline SVG markup, a cross-origin asset). Each has a reason and, when it applies, the state and node it concerns.

05.8Pages, crawls and navigation since 0.2.0

A scan may crawl same-origin links breadth-first. Each crawled page is an app.pages[] entry with its depth from the seed and discoveredVia, the navigation edge that led there; its base states carry the page's pageId. Navigation edges to crawled pages have followed: true and a pageId; cross-origin edges are recorded with sameOrigin: false and never followed. A transition whose click led to another crawled page carries navigation: { toPageId, url } and points at a base state of that page. Pages share a SharedLayout when their landmark regions agree structurally, and a component candidate that appears on several pages lists them in pageIds. Per-page coverage records how many interactive elements were discovered, how many interactions were attempted, how many changed the page and how many were skipped.

05.9Forms since 0.2.0

Form controls carry form facts: native validity, the browser's validation message when invalid, required, the control type and whether a value was present. Values of sensitive controls are never stored, and the explorer only ever types synthetic values. With the forms exploration policy, fill actions (with the synthetic value) and submit actions produce derived states that show client-side validation; the submission request itself is blocked and the transition is marked sideEffects: true. A11yProps.invalid and errorMessage expose the accessibility view of the same facts.

05.10Data assets since 0.2.0

When a scan opts into captureBodies: "json", JSON responses of XHR and fetch requests become assets of kind data: a redacted copy under localPath, the request that produced them and measured / network provenance. Generators turn them into typed, labeled mocks; no backend is ever implied.

05.11Breakpoints and responsive rules since 0.3.0

visual.responsive says where the layout changes, which the scanned widths alone cannot tell. The scan reads the width conditions of the page's readable stylesheets (@media, an @import media list, a <link media>) into conditions, each with its thresholds: the smallest viewport width of the wider side, so (max-width: 599px) and (min-width: 600px) both flip at 600. A print condition is never; parts the parser could not convert to pixels are listed as unsupported. Cross-origin stylesheets cannot be read and are reported as limitations.

Probing then resizes the page between the scanned widths, with no other interaction and every non-GET request blocked, and compares a layout signature (rendered or not, display, position, flex-direction, float, grid track count). A stylesheet threshold inside a changing interval is confirmed one pixel apart; any remaining change is bisected within a budget. Each located change is a breakpoint with minWidth, the bracket that located it (lower < minWidth <= upper), and source: "css" when a condition explains it or "probe" when none does. rules list the layout properties of each node that change there, with their values below and above; properties the signature leaves out (sizes, fonts, colors) are added from the two captures around a stylesheet threshold when the condition's rules declare them. observedEffect on a condition is false when probing saw no change at its threshold and null when no probe reached it (a threshold above the widest scanned width). probes record the widths measured per page.

Breakpoint tokens in visual.tokens.breakpoints keep their 0.2.0 meaning: observed differences between scanned widths.

05.12Collections since 0.3.0

collections.definitions lists repeated items measured in each page's widest base state: table rows, list items, card grids. A collection names its container, the item identity (an identity attribute such as data-id, else a digest of the item's text, never a node path), its fields (table columns with their header text, or text-bearing parts present in most items) with a valueKind (number, date, text), and the items in base order with their displayed values.

collections.rules classify observed transitions by item identity against the base items: search (a fill on a search control left a subset, with the match and the fields that explain both the kept and the removed items), filter (a control left a subset; the predicate is a field equals or contains the control's label, else the observed membership in-keys), sort (same items, new order; the field, direction and comparator that explain it, and the aria-sort the page showed) and reset (back to the base view). Each rule keeps the views before and after, and the empty-state message shown when no item remained. Rules are observed; an agent's reading of them belongs in annotations.

05.13Versioning

dnaVersion follows semver. Readers accept documents of the same major version. Additions within a major are backwards compatible; removals or meaning changes bump the major. See packages/schema/CHANGELOG.md.
